data.concept: base case and recursive case correctness
evidence: The recursive case uses `factorial(n + 1)` instead of `factorial(n - 1)`, causing the argument to increase with each recursive call rather than decrease toward the base case.
Since n starts at 5 and grows with each call (6, 7, 8, ...), the base case `n == 0 or n == 1` will never be reached, resulting in infinite recursion.
data.invariant: Each recursive call must move the problem state closer to the base case (i.e., the argument must converge toward the base case condition).
